name: Lexical Chain Fixation
description: Analyzes the diversity and repetition of 'lexical chains' (sequences of topically related words). AI models frequently hyper-fixate on a narrow set of thematic vocabulary, endlessly recycling the same words or highly predictable synonyms rather than organically expanding the semantic field.
algorithm: Topical Vocabulary Extraction & Chain Redundancy Scoring
mechanism: A 'lexical chain' is a sequence of related words that runs through a text, providing cohesion (e.g., 'hospital' -> 'doctor' -> 'surgery' -> 'recovery'). When humans write a long document, their lexical chains naturally wander, branch out, and incorporate highly diverse, multi-layered vocabulary derived from personal experience or lateral thinking. Conversely, Large Language Models operate on fixed attention mechanisms and probability distributions. Once an LLM anchors onto a specific topic, it gets 'trapped' in a narrow semantic neighborhood. It will extract the top 10 most probable words for that topic and simply cycle through them continuously. This creates a dense, highly repetitive lexical chain where the exact same nouns and verbs reappear with unnatural frequency. This algorithm maps all thematic word sequences in the document and calculates the ratio of unique chain entities to total chain occurrences. If a text discusses a complex topic for 500 words but relies on recycling the exact same 5 thematic words instead of branching out, it strongly indicates AI-generated semantic stagnation.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing essays, blog posts, and articles where a human writer would naturally demonstrate an expansive, evolving vocabulary, whereas an AI would just repeat the prompt's keywords.
strengths:
• Excellent at exposing 'semantic looping'—the AI habit of talking in circles using the same vocabulary when forced to meet a length requirement without having new information to add.
• Highly resilient to minor edits, as human editors rarely rewrite the entire underlying thematic vocabulary web of a document.
• Catches the fundamental difference between human associative memory (broad) and AI attention windows (narrowly focused on highest-probability tokens).
limitations:
• Less effective on highly technical, scientific, or legal documents where the repetition of exact terminology (strict lexical chains) is mandatory for precision and clarity (yielding a high false positive rate).
• Requires longer texts to accurately map a chain; analyzing lexical chains in a 50-word paragraph is statistically meaningless.
• Computationally heavier than basic n-gram analysis due to the required semantic relationship mapping.
parameters:
Analysis: Thematic Grouping & Repetition Frequency Mapping
Metric: Unique Chain Nodes / Total Chain Mentions
Output: 0-100 Lexical Stagnation (Chain Fixation) Score
accuracy: High — 81-87% on creative and generalized non-fiction texts. It provides a robust structural map of an AI's limited thematic imagination.

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
